key_insight: Neutron-irradiated CdS/CdTe solar cells show persistent performance losses after 18 months, while mild illuminated annealing provides only partial recovery.
engineering_relevance: Radiation-tolerant CdTe space photovoltaics require coordinated optimization of the glass, absorber, and contacts because annealing can improve photocurrent while degrading fill factor.
method: Irradiated cells in a 90 kW TRIGA reactor for 10–150 min, reaching nominal neutron fluences of 3.3 × 10^14–5.0 × 10^15 n/cm².
Characterized devices and co-irradiated FTO-coated glass after 18 months of storage.
Evaluated recovery through annealing at 70 °C under one-sun illumination.
evidence_signal: Glass transmittance at 500 nm fell from 80% to 50% after 60 min of irradiation; annealed cells reached their highest efficiency after 4 h, followed by substantial fill-factor degradation with longer annealing.
watch_item: Measurements after long-term storage do not establish immediate radiation damage or recovery kinetics, and the underlying defect mechanisms remain unresolved.
paper_title: Persistent Neutron Irradiation Effects and Partial Recovery in Thin-Film CdS/CdTe Solar Cells
